items.title: A characterisation of separated formal algebraic spaces through fibre products of affines

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states the equivalence of two conditions for a formal algebraic space: that its reduction is a separated algebraic space, and that for any two morphisms from affine schemes into the space the fibre product is affine and the natural map from the tensor product of the two coordinate rings to its coordinate ring is surjective (statement lines 3609-3624). One direction is short: the second condition applied to the reduction gives separatedness there, using the identification of the fibre products over the space and over its reduction (proof lines 3626-3631). The other direction is a genuine argument. Given the first condition and two affine morphisms, the fibre product is first seen to be a scheme; the reduction of the fibre product is identified with the reduction of the fibre product of the two reductions, which is affine with surjective comparison map by the corresponding characterisation for algebraic spaces, so the fibre product itself is affine (proof lines 3633-3650). Then the map from that fibre product to the product of the two affine schemes is factored as a monomorphism locally of finite type followed by an immersion, and shown to be integral because on reduced affine schemes it is a closed immersion; the induced ring map is therefore an integral finite type epimorphism, hence finite, hence surjective (proof lines 3650-3683). The claim is H3: after the short direction, the proof combines an identification of reductions, a criterion taking an algebraic space to an affine scheme, and a chain of properties of the comparison morphism ending in an algebra statement, so at least three independent mechanisms are used.
